en.title: The Fragmentation We Call a System
en.abstract: Thirteen jurisdictions, a dozen vendors, and no shared record. A survey of how Canada actually runs its clinical information systems today, and what fragmentation costs in dollars and in care.

en.title: Renting Sovereignty: The Foreign Vendor Problem
en.abstract: What happens when the company that holds a province's patient records restructures, gets acquired, or is compelled by a foreign government — and why 'not now' is not the same as 'never'.

en.title: What We Don't Have to Build Twice
en.abstract: An assessment of OpenMRS, Bahmni, and openEHR as candidate foundations, and why Canada should extend rather than replace the interoperability work Infoway has already funded.

en.title: One Spine, Many Modules
en.abstract: A technical architecture where each jurisdiction owns a module, every module speaks CA Core+ FHIR, and no province is blocked on another's delivery schedule.

en.title: Who Holds the Pen
en.abstract: A governance model for a federal-provincial-territorial consortium that can make binding technical decisions without recreating the health-transfer disputes of the last thirty years.

en.title: The Mandated Contribution Model
en.abstract: How a shared-cost formula, tied to existing federal health transfers, could fund development once instead of thirteen times — and what happens to the money provinces already pay Oracle and Epic.

en.title: Ten Years, Thirteen Jurisdictions
en.abstract: A realistic delivery sequence: which province goes first, which module ships first, and how the system stays useful at every step rather than only at the end.
